cards.text: Psalm 91 doesn't name its writer, but he opens with a promise: whoever dwells in the shelter of the Most High will abide in the shadow of the Almighty. Shelter AND shadow, friend! My last shelter was a junk drawer, and my only shadow was a takeout menu.

cards.question: Then the psalm writer speaks for himself, straight to the LORD. What does he call Him?

cards.text: Then he turns to you, the listener: surely God will deliver you from the snare of the fowler and from the deadly plague. A trap AND a plague? That's a ROUGH week, friend, and the psalm says God gets you out of both.

Next the psalm paints a picture of how God protects you: He will cover you with His feathers. Friend, I pack cookie boxes with my mustache, but covering somebody with FEATHERS? That's a whole other level.

cards.question: Under His wings you will find refuge, the psalm says. It also calls God's faithfulness a shield.

cards.text: Next the psalm says you will not fear the terror of the night. Friend, I spent YEARS in a dark drawer, so the night and I have history.

cards.question: The only thing the psalm says you won't fear is what comes at night.

cards.text: The list keeps going: the arrow that flies by day, the pestilence that stalks in the darkness, the calamity that destroys at noon. That's a LONG list of trouble, friend. Longer than the pile of old receipts in my junk drawer.

cards.question: The psalm keeps naming more things you won't fear. What's the big picture?

answers.text: There's no hour you need to fear
Stay inside where it's safe after dark
Only the bravest make it through the day

cards.text: Then the numbers get big. A thousand may fall at your side, and ten thousand at your right hand.

cards.question: Though a thousand may fall at your side and ten thousand at your right hand, the psalm says no harm will come near you.
Thousands may fall, but no harm will come near you. The psalm says you will only see it with your eyes and witness the ___ of the wicked.

cards.text: More big promises: no evil will befall you, no plague will approach your tent. And this time, the psalm tells you why.

cards.question: The psalm says no evil will befall you. What reason does it give?

answers.text: You've made the LORD your home
You've moved far from any danger

cards.question: Then the psalm says God sends help. He will command His ___ concerning you to guard you in all your ways.

cards.text: They will lift you up in their hands, so that you will not strike your foot against a stone. Me? I stub my gold base on the oven door EVERY morning, so I'll take all the lifting I can get.

cards.question: Lions and cobras usually mean danger. What does the psalm say you'll do to them?

cards.text: Then the voice changes. Now the LORD Himself is speaking about one person, and I'd take my hat off, but then I'd just be a mustache on a base.

cards.question: The LORD says He will deliver this person. Why?

answers.text: Because he is stronger than others

cards.question: The LORD gives a second reason too. He says He will protect this person because he knows His name.

cards.text: The LORD keeps going: when this person calls out to Him, He will answer. No hold music, friend. No 'your call is important to us.'

cards.question: The LORD answers the one who loves Him when he calls. Then He makes a promise about trouble. What is it?

answers.text: He'll be with him in it
He'll warn him before it comes
He'll teach him to face it alone

cards.text: Two more promises in that same line: He will deliver him and honor him.
Then the LORD promises this: with long life He will satisfy him.

cards.question: After all the delivering in this psalm, the LORD names one more thing He'll do for the one who loves Him: show him My ___.

findings.problem: Story cards 3, 4 and 8 each have three sentences rather than one or two. Cards 3 and 4 each use a retelling followed by two separate joke sentences, and card 8 follows its retelling with two separate sentences about the long list and the receipts.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card cites only verse 10, but its statement that the psalm now tells you why also uses the 'Because' clause in verse 9. Its citation does not include every verse the card uses.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: Neither the earlier cards nor the setup 'God sends help' gives the baker a way to reason out 'angels' rather than 'prophets' or 'priests'. The blank tests unseen wording by luck instead of a meaning established by the setup.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Story cards 4 and 9 each have three sentences rather than one or two. In card 4, 'Me?' is a separate sentence between the retelling and the oven joke; card 9 has the retelling followed by 'No hold music, friend.' and the separate call-center line.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
